members.title: UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea
members.lead: Decision was widely expected after lobbying by Shell but will dismay environmental campaigners What does the UK’s approval of the Jackdaw gasfield mean? UK politics live – latest updates Business live – latest updates The UK government has approved the controversial Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea, a widely expected move that will nonetheless dismay environmental campaigners and a number of Labour MPs. While Labour’s 2024 election manifesto committed to a ban on new drilling licences in the North Sea, the companies behind Jackdaw and the Rosebank oilfield project, which is being decided on separately, have sought environmental approval for existing licences. Continue reading...

members.title: Climate campaigners condemn ‘maddening’ decision to approve Jackdaw gasfield
members.lead: Critics say move will jeopardise climate targets, fail to cut cost of living and distract from need to decarbonise energy UK politics live – latest updates Climate campaigners and green experts have condemned the government’s decision to allow the drilling of the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea. They said approval for the site would jeopardise the UK’s climate targets, fail to reduce the cost of living, and distract from the need to decarbonise the UK’s energy sector. Continue reading...

members.title: Labour accused of ‘climate vandalism’ by Green leader Polanski after Jackdaw gasfield approved – UK politics live
members.lead: The Jackdaw field will start supplying gas to homes and businesses from the end of the month, the government said In her interviews this morning, Miatta Fahnbulleh confirmed that approving the Jackdaw gasfield would not lead to cheaper energy bills for consumers. On LBC Nick Ferrari asked if the decision meant that his listeners would have lower bills. Fahnbulleh replied: No, and I think it’s really important that we’re honest about this. That was not a consideration in the decision because it won’t mean cheaper bills. This was about energy security and having homegrown energy, and it was also because we thought it was compatible with our with our climate commitments. Continue reading...
